name: Vector Tennis
tagline: 4,022 ATP and WTA player-seasons built from 67,081 matches, with a mask that stops a player who never played grass from looking like they lost every grass match.
dims: 16 masked features x 4,022 rows — no tennis tower is trained yet; unified_meta.json sport_dim lists only hoops 64, gridiron 32, pitch 24

insights.title: The sponsor was sitting in the tournament's name the whole time
insights.body: A prior feasibility doc recorded the tennis sponsor rationale as failed at 0.29% of tournaments — but that figure measures Wikidata's P859 property, a sparse editorial field, not sponsorship. Reading the tournament names already present in the downloaded spreadsheets instead: 162 of 307 tournament-location pairs (52.8%) carry a candidate sponsor token, and 60 of 169 locations (35.5%) show a token that arrives or departs at a fixed venue. 36 tokens survive the CONFIRMED conjunction of a company-name match AND a dated rename. The strongest single piece of evidence is cross-venue synchrony: 'aegon' sits on Birmingham 2013-2018 and Eastbourne 2013-2017, then 'viking' appears at both venues in 2021 and in no other year at either.

insights.title: Six clusters, and five of them are just quality tiers
insights.body: k-means at k=6 on the 16 features returns a tiering, not a taxonomy. PC1 carries 0.3748 of the variance and loads on WIN_RATE (0.41), DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN (0.402) and GAMES_WON_PCT (0.397) — that is 'how good', not 'what kind'. Exactly one cluster reads as a role: cluster 4, n=487, where quality is flat (max |z| = 0.271) and SURFACE_SPECIALISATION sits at z = +1.655. The probe file deliberately proposes no archetype names, on the grounds that labelling a k-means partition would launder it into a taxonomy.

insights.title: Half the surface columns are missing on purpose
insights.body: GRASS_WR is observed on only 2,235 of 4,022 rows (55.6%) and INDOOR_WR on 2,065 (51.3%), because a surface win rate is masked below 3 matches on that surface rather than zero-filled. The stated reason is blunt: a player who never played grass did not lose every grass match. Eight of the sixteen features are 100% observed; the other eight carry a mask, including UPSET_RATE at 99.0% and HOLD_RATE at 95.5%.

insights.title: A ranking is made of results, so it has to be lagged
insights.body: Correlating a same-season ranking against that same season's win rate returns 0.7527 on ATP and 0.675 on WTA — largely results correlated with themselves. Using the previous season's median rank instead drops those to 0.6088 and 0.4962, a shrinkage of 0.191 and 0.265 respectively. Both numbers are reported side by side on purpose: a lag that failed to shrink anything would mean the lag never removed the contamination it exists to remove.

insights.title: The canonical free tennis dataset no longer exists
insights.body: Measured 2026-08-03: JeffSackmann/tennis_atp and tennis_wta both 404 on main and master, and api.github.com reports public_repos=1 for that account. This corpus is rebuilt from tennis-data.co.uk's free per-season spreadsheets instead — 28 seasons requested, 28 present, 67,081 matches, of which 67,080 (100.0%) carry a full pre-match ranking prior and 67,012 (99.9%) carry closing odds. No key, no paid API.

game.prompt: Which season did the model see going deeper into draws?
game.axis_label: DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN — mean round reached per tournament entered
game.explainer: DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN is the average round a player reached across every tournament they entered that season: 1.0 means going out in the first round everywhere, 7.0 is the top of the observed scale. It is observed on all 4,022 rows and is the single most discriminating feature in the matrix (cluster spread 2.631).

rounds.reveal: Barty's 2022 row is 11 matches and 11 wins, and mean draw progress lands on 7.0 — the top of the observed scale. Djokovic's 88-match, 82-win 2015 reads 6.875 because the average is spread over far more tournaments.
Near-identical workloads — 77 matches and 65 wins against 78 and 67 — and the model separates the two seasons by 0.0588 of a round.
Same season, and the model has Murray about a quarter of a round deeper: 79 matches and 71 wins against Djokovic's 72 and 64.
Federer's 2017 has the far better win ratio (53 wins from 58 matches) but the model still rates his 80-match 2014 higher at 6.1765 — this axis is depth per event entered, not the ratio.
Cross-tour and 0.0286 apart. Williams played 41 matches for 36 wins in 2016, Sinner 78 for 71 in 2024, and the per-event averages land within a thirty-fifth of a round of each other.
The model puts Alcaraz's 2022 nearly a full round deeper than his 2024 — 67 matches and 55 wins against 56 and 44 — because the mean counts every event entered, shallow ones included.
Halep's 26-match 2020 reads a full round deeper than her 57-match 2018. The truncated calendar is visible in the corpus itself: the WTA 2020 file holds 1,055 matches against 2,469 in 2018.
The model rates Gauff's 2024 above her 2025 — 5.0 against 4.2941 — on 68 matches and 52 wins versus 60 and 44.
Thiem's 31-match 2020 averages 5.4286 rounds against Nadal's 4.6667 across 49 matches in 2016 — a short season of deep runs outranks a longer one on a per-event axis.
Same season, different tours, 0.0174 of a round apart: Rybakina's 72 matches and 53 wins average marginally deeper than Djokovic's 50 and 39.

caveat: No serve or shot statistics exist in this source — no aces, first-serve percentage, winners or unforced errors. The classic big-server vs baseline-grinder style axis is therefore NOT derivable here and is not faked. What is derivable is behavioural: surface specialisation, upset vs hold rate, decider rate, margin. (verbatim from tennis_matrix_report.json → not_derivable)
